paragraphs: Here's what I want you to carry out of that cave, friend. David had the chance, the cheering section and the king sitting there helpless. His men even said this was the day the LORD spoke of (1 Samuel 24:4). But David said, "The LORD forbid that I should do such a thing to my master, the LORD's anointed" (1 Samuel 24:6), and he held his men back.

So what did David do with his hurt? He handed it to the LORD. "May the LORD judge between you and me," he said, "but my hand will never be against you" (1 Samuel 24:12). Friend, that is HARD. When somebody wrongs you, everything in you wants to settle the score right now, and I once spent years in a drawer without a single chance to settle anything. Trusting the LORD to be the judge means you can keep your hands clean even while the wrong is still happening.

And look what that clean-handed choice did. Saul wept and said, "You are more righteous than I" (1 Samuel 24:17), and then he said out loud that David would be king (1 Samuel 24:20). But hear me, baker: David didn't spare Saul to get that speech. He did it because it was right. The story isn't over, so keep your oven warm.
